The bolt catfish, Aguarunichthys torosus, is a pimelodid catfish known only from the Río Marañón in the upper Amazon basin of Peru. It probably also occurs in some tributaries draining into Peru from Ecuador. Also traded as 'Jello Band' or 'Yellow Band' catfish, it eats fishes small enough to fit in its mouth and is aggressively territorial towards conspecifics, so is best kept singly among larger, ideally fluvial, species.

  • Max size: 346 mm SL (14 in SL)
  • Needs a very large tank

This species is known only from the Río Marañón in the upper Amazon basin, Peru, and probably occurs in some tributaries draining into Peru from Ecuador.

Type locality is 'Río Cenepa, Departo. Amazonas, Peru, about 4°28'S, 78°10'W, elevation about 210 meters'.

An obligate predator feeding on other fishes in nature, but quality dried foods are normally accepted in captivity.

It should also be offered meaty fare such as strips of white fish, live earthworms, shrimp, etc., for optimal health.

Adult individuals are unlikely to require feeding on a daily basis with 2-3 meals per week sufficient.
Will take dry food pellets, earthworms or fish fillet. Earthworms are perhaps the best staple.

This species will eat fishes small enough to fit in its capacious mouth and is aggressively territorial towards conspecifics so is best-maintained as a single specimen in a community of larger, ideally fluvial, species.

A predator that will eat anything small enough. A loner, shows considerable intra-species aggression around a large territory.

Tankmates must be large enough to not to be considered edible. Competition for food is not an issue, this species is a capable hunter.
This species is also traded as 'Jello Band' or 'Yellow Band' catfish.
Etymology: Aguarun = Peruvian Indian tribe that lives in Ecuador, and "ichthys" = Greek for fish.
